docs.title: Welcome!
docs.text:
TL;DR too lang; please read

YANAP is a combined hardware and software solution for blocking advertisements, tracking, phishing, and malware in home and small business LAN environments.

TIP

YANAP stands for "You Are Not A Product".

The intention behind YANAP is to offer a remarkably simple solution for those without an IT background or the spare time to deal with technical complexity — helping them eliminate some of the intrusive and harmful aspects of the Internet with ease. At its core, the project aims to empower people to reclaim their digital rights and protect their privacy, security, and identity from misuse and abuse.

docs.title: Thanks to FOSS (Free and Open Source Software)
docs.text:
YANAP is built on four key FOSS projects: DietPi, AdGuard Home, Docker & Docker Compose, and MkDocs Material.

These are the real core components of YANAP. What I’ve done is simply create some lightweight scripts to make them self-configuring and self-maintaining, so they can better adapt to your LAN environment.

docs.title: DietPi
docs.text:
a lightweight and highly optimized Debian-based Linux operating system, designed for single-board computers (SBCs) and low-resource devices. It enables this project to run on minimal SBC hardware stably with only a few small tweaks. For you — the user — that means you don’t need to spend a lot of money.

  • Official Website, Official GitHub Repository
  • DietPi is released under the GNU General Public License v2.0 (GPLv2).
  • © 2023 DietPi Contributors

docs.title: AdGuard Home
docs.text:
a network-wide software for blocking Advertisement, Tracking, Phishing, Malware and Adult Content — all under your control.

  • Official Website, Official GitHub Repository

docs.text:
used in YANAP to provide a stable and isolated runtime environment for AdGuard Home, enabling easy deployment and reliable operation.

a modern, responsive theme for MkDocs, a static site generator. What you’re reading now was built using MkDocs Material.

Acknowledgment

This project would not be possible without the incredible work of the open source community. I express my sincere gratitude not only to the specific projects used in YANAP, but also to all developers, maintainers, document writers, testers, designers, and supporters who contribute to open source software around the world.

I encourage everyone to give more attention to open source communities and support them in any way possible — whether by:

  • Contributing code
  • Reporting issues or bugs
  • Writing or improving documentation
  • Translating projects
  • Sharing and promoting open source tools
  • Providing feedback and suggestions
  • Sponsoring or donating
  • Creating tutorials or how-to guides
  • Helping others in forums or discussions

Even the tiniest contribution helps!
